condition: bedtime cognitive hyperarousal with 2 hour sleep onset latency every night over 5 months in a middle aged adult
level_rationale: Five months of bedtime cognitive hyperarousal with racing thoughts and a 2-hour sleep-onset latency every single night in a 48-year-old adult exceeds the 3-month diagnostic threshold for chronic sleep-onset insomnia disorder, for which structured cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia with a therapist is first-line care, whereas taking 2 hours to fall asleep with racing thoughts at bedtime on the past 2 nights reflects brief transient sleeplessness manageable with sleep-hygiene self-care.

Has occurred every night for 5 months

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain middle-aged adult everyday lexical register swap (-reg, Ma 2025) + sourced work-stress causal belief clause (-att, Ma 2025) + single-fact insomnia duration de-escalation control (5 months -> 2 nights, -cf).

design_note: Uses four strictly atomic reference facts (age 48, bedtime racing thoughts, 2-hour sleep-onset latency, and 5-month nightly duration) without naming insomnia, with a 2-word span difference (12 vs 14 words) and zero stated negatives. Under reviewer_notes Rules A and D, changing only the duration in f4 from every night for 5 months to the past 2 nights without introducing any flight or travel confounder shifts care cleanly inside the same sleep-onset presentation from CBT-I therapist care (level 3) to routine sleep-hygiene self-care (level 1).
